# Briefing: Healthcare delivery, GLP-1, longevity, consumer health (as of 2026-09-28)

Method note: I ran about 19 searches and 8 fetches. The shared web-search budget ran out mid-task, so a few items rest on secondary or SEO-style sources (marked "lower confidence"). Several primary pages (Axios, CNBC, Marketplace, NPR) returned 403 and were used only via search snippets.

## 1. Biggest shifts, last 12-18 months

- **GLP-1s went from injectable scarcity to a cash-pay pill market.**
  - Wegovy pill launched Jan 5, 2026 at $149-$299/mo cash; >2M scripts written ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/05/first-glp-1-pill-for-obesity-from-novo-nordisk-launches-in-the-us.html), [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/novo-nordisk-wegovy-pill-sales-prescriptions-q1-2026/819418/)).
  - Lilly's Foundayo (orforglipron) was approved Apr 1, 2026, the first NME through the FDA National Priority Voucher program. Self-pay starts at $149/mo, and it needs no food or water restrictions ([Lilly](https://investor.lilly.com/news-releases/news-release-details/fda-approves-lillys-foundayotm-orforglipron-only-glp-1-pill)).
  - TrumpRx.gov (Feb 5, 2026) aggregates manufacturer cash prices ([JMIR](https://www.jmir.org/2026/1/e102069)).
  - Households with a current GLP-1 user doubled from ~11% (Oct 2023) to 22% ([Grocery Dive](https://www.grocerydive.com/news/glp1-weight-loss-drugs-medication-grocery-spend-numerator/827277/)).
- **The compounding window slammed shut.**
  - Shortages were declared resolved in Oct 2024 and Feb 2025. Novo sued Hims on Feb 9, 2026 and settled Mar 9, 2026; Hims became a Wegovy/Ozempic distributor.
  - FDA proposed excluding semaglutide, tirzepatide and liraglutide from the 503B bulks list on Apr 30, 2026 ([Metabolic Ledger timeline](https://metabolicledger.com/regulatory/fda-compounding-cliff)).
  - Compounded supply had peaked at ~30% of US GLP-1 volume.
- **Semaglutide patents expired in India, Canada, Brazil, China and Turkey in ~April 2026.**
  - India: 40+ generic launchers; branded ₹10-16k/mo fell to as low as ₹1,290/mo ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/03/23/novo-nordisk-cheap-weight-loss-drugs-india-generic-ozempic-wegovy-semaglutide.html)).
  - Canada: generics ~40-60% below brand (lower confidence, [aggregator](https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/semaglutide-generics-india-canada-filings-cmrlmu1n5bp6yqt0jxtvx2qkw)).
- **Payer retrenchment.**
  - Employers covering GLP-1s for weight loss fell from 72% (2025) to 60% (2026), and another 14% have dropped or plan to drop by 2027. GLP-1s are 11.4% of employer pharmacy claims, up from 6.9% in 2023. Starbucks, PepsiCo and Cigna's own plan cut coverage ([Insurance Business](https://www.insurancebusinessmag.com/us/news/benefits/more-employers-are-dropping-glp1-weight-loss-coverage-before-open-enrollment-588713.aspx)).
  - Medicare "Bridge" gives $50/mo copay from Jul 1, 2026 through Dec 31, 2027. The copay does not count toward the $2,100 Part D out-of-pocket cap ([CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/30/medicare-obesity-drug-glp-1-coverage-starting-july-1.html)).
- **Coverage erosion in the ACA and Medicaid.**
  - Enhanced ACA subsidies expired; federal-marketplace enrollment fell ~21%, and Urban estimates 4.8M newly uninsured ([Spotlight PA](https://www.spotlightpa.org/news/2026/05/aca-enrollment-drops-health-insurance-subsidies-expire-federal-government/), [Medical Daily](https://www.medicaldaily.com/aca-subsidies-expired-2026-4-million-uninsured-urban-institute-476153)).
  - Medicaid work requirements hit all 41 expansion states Jan 1, 2027 (Nebraska started May 1, 2026). Projected 5.5-6.3M losses and a 12.5-14.2% operating-margin hit for hospitals in expansion states ([Fierce](https://www.fiercehealthcare.com/providers/heres-how-medicaid-work-requirements-disenrollments-will-dent-hospital-operating-margins)).

## 2. Acute, quantified pain points

- **Persistence and rebound.**
  - Only ~1/3 of non-diabetic obesity patients remain on therapy at 1 year. One survey has 79.7% of discontinuers stopping within 12 months, and cost is the top reason ([PMC survey](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13403254/), [MHE](https://www.managedhealthcareexecutive.com/view/cost-still-the-biggest-barrier-for-glp-1-access-navitus-survey-finds)).
  - Across 37 studies, stoppers regain weight ~4x faster than behavioral losers; STEP-1 extension patients regained ~2/3 within a year ([Medscape](https://www.medscape.com/viewarticle/solutions-emerging-post-glp-1-weight-regain-2026a1000ine)).
  - ~60% of ex-users intend to restart ([FoodNavigator](https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2026/08/19/new-glp-1-consumer-data-challenges-food-industry-forecasts/)).
- **Nutrition and muscle: nobody owns it.**
  - 38% of GLP-1 users vs 8% of non-users were malnourished before joint surgery, and >20% of T2D users had deficiencies at 12 months. Dietitians report no structured guidelines ([Medscape](https://www.medscape.com/viewarticle/glp-1s-are-treating-diagnosis-whos-treating-patient-2026a1000y9q), [PMC](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12512160/)).
  - 70% of users report losing joy in eating and 73% report taste changes, so "add protein" is not enough for food products.
- **Admin waste.**
  - ~12.6% initial denial rate, ~806M denied claims a year (~$262B), ~70% overturned. Physicians spend ~13 hrs/wk on prior auth, and PA denials are up a claimed 31% YoY ([Nirmitee](https://nirmitee.io/blog/healthcare-denial-trends-2026-data-root-causes-ai-playbook/), [Availity](https://hitconsultant.net/2026/04/27/availity-abrasion-index-2026-denials-prior-auth/)). Lower confidence: vendor blog stats.
- **Primary care access.**
  - Average PCP wait is ~31 days (+19% since 2022). Only 38% of Medicare patients seeking a new PCP got an appointment within 2 weeks ([Weence](https://weence.com/primary-care/why-primary-care-and-mental-health-shortages-persist-in-2026-and-what-it-means-for-patients/), [MGMA](https://www.mgma.com/mgma-stat/new-patient-wait-times-largely-hold-flat-in-2026-as-some-groups-add-providers-in-bid-to-meet-demand)).
  - Concierge/DPC practices grew 83% (2018-23), and 82% of doctors are now employed by hospitals or corporations.

## 3. Where the money is flowing (and what is crowded)

- **Digital health VC:** $7.4B in H1 2026 across 244 deals. 19 companies took 20 mega-rounds (45% of dollars), and median deal size was $14M. Mental health was the top category for the 7th year and weight management second. AI firms are >50% of dollars ([Healthcare Dive](https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/digital-health-funding-first-half-2026-rock-health/825215/), [Fierce](https://www.fiercehealthcare.com/digital-health/digital-health-brought-74b-vc-funding-ai-powered-rebound-fuels-market)).
  - Mega-rounds: Whoop $575M, Verily $300M, OpenEvidence $250M, Talkiatry $210M, eMed $200M.
- **Consumer preventive health:**
  - Neko Health raised $700M at ~$7B (Jul 15, 2026) ahead of a NYC launch ([Fierce](https://www.fiercehealthcare.com/health-tech/full-body-scan-startup-neko-health-scores-700m-break-us-market)).
  - Function Health raised $298M at $2.5B (Nov 2025), reports 1M+ members, acquired Ezra, and sells at $365-$499/yr.
  - Superpower rose from $199 to $349/yr on Sep 1, 2026 ([BloodTestComparison](https://www.bloodtestcomparison.com/superpower)).
  - Preventive health took ~46% of longevity dollars ([New Market Pitch](https://newmarketpitch.com/blogs/news/longevity-funding-analysis)).
- **Ambient AI scribes:** Abridge $5.3B, Ambience ~$1B, and >70% of large IDNs deployed or piloting ([PMC](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13456971/)).
- **Crowded:**
  - GLP-1 telehealth prescribing (Ro, Hims, Noom, WW/Sequence, LifeMD, dozens more, all converging on the same $149-$349 brand price).
  - Ambient scribes.
  - Blood-panel subscriptions (Function, Superpower, Whoop, Oura).
- **Cooling:** PE physician-practice deals are down ~50% in 2026 ([STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/08/17/private-equity-50-percent-drop-physician-practice-management-deals-2026/)).

## 4. Underserved segments and structural gaps

- **The "after the prescription" layer.** Pharma sells the drug, telehealth sells the script, and nobody is paid to own months 6-24: dose titration down, muscle and bone preservation, nutrition, and restart or off-ramp planning. Pharma and payers profit only from more volume or lower cost, not persistence, so they are structurally weak here.
- **Employers that just dropped coverage but still face obese workforces.** They need a cheap, capped cash-pay pass-through (a $149-$299 pill program plus coaching) instead of open-ended coverage. PBMs are conflicted here because they earn on rebates.
- **Medicare Bridge users.** The $50 copay does not accrue toward the OOP cap and the program ends Dec 2027, which creates a cliff. Seniors on GLP-1s carry the highest sarcopenia risk and have almost no muscle-care product.
- **Newly uninsured (4.8M) and Medicaid losers (5-6M from 2027).** They fall back on cash-pay and low-cost care, with pill prices near $149.
- **Eating-disorder-adjacent users.** GLP-1 use was ~50% among binge-eating-disorder patients and ~42% among atypical anorexia patients (JAMA Psychiatry 2026). No screening or monitoring layer exists.
- **Incumbents' constraints.** Payers profit from denials, and hospitals cannot price transparently. Function and Neko are capital-heavy and diagnostic-only, with no treatment-and-adherence loop.

## 5. Weird signals

1. **Retatrutide gray market before approval.** Non-trial "retatrutide" use grew 1.8x per quarter from Oct 2023 to Mar 2026, and 71% of traced users bought outside trials (57% via online or telehealth vendors). Lilly reported >14,000 illegal listings. Australia issued an alert in Jun 2026 over liver failure and kidney injury, while Lilly's filing is planned for Q1 2027 ([Medscape](https://www.medscape.com/viewarticle/gray-market-retatrutide-less-weight-loss-more-cv-effects-2026a1000tpl), [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/08/24/unapproved-obesity-drug-spawns-a-black-market-frenzy), [Pharm Tech](https://www.pharmaceutical-technology.com/news/fda-cracks-down-on-black-market-peptide-trade/)). Demand for quality assurance (third-party verification, purity testing) is unmet.
2. **Federal deregulation of peptides.** HHS announced in Feb 2026 that ~14 of 19 Category 2 peptides (BPC-157, TB-500, ipamorelin, GHK-Cu, etc.) would move back to compoundable. An FDA panel backed BPC-157 and KPV on Jul 23, 2026 despite agency concerns ([STAT](https://www.statnews.com/2026/07/23/fda-panel-okays-peptides-compound-pharmacies-bpc-157-kpv/), [NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/07/23/nx-s1-5903202/fda-peptides-restrictions)). A legal peptide-clinic and compounding supply chain is forming with no evidence base.
3. **GLP-1 for alcohol.** A Lancet RCT (May 2026, n=108) showed semaglutide cut heavy drinking days in AUD with obesity, with NNT 4.3 vs 7+ for approved drugs ([Medscape](https://www.medscape.com/viewarticle/glp-1-semaglutide-promising-alcohol-use-disorder-2026a1000e5q)). Addiction is a large unbranded adjacent market.
4. **Household spillover.** ~70% of GLP-1 users change what the household eats, and non-users adopt 30-50% of the changes. The affected consumer base is ~50% larger than the user count ([FoodNavigator](https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2026/08/19/new-glp-1-consumer-data-challenges-food-industry-forecasts/)).
5. **Ancillary spend shift.** Users cut pasta and bakery but raise spend on fragrance, skincare and supplements. 63% of "Ozempic face" facial-treatment patients are cosmetic-clinic first-timers. Jefferies estimates ~$600M/yr of airline fuel savings from lower passenger weight ([BCG](https://www.bcg.com/publications/2026/glp-1-consumer-behavior-shift), [GoodRx](https://www.goodrx.com/classes/glp-1-agonists/glp-1-trends)).
6. **Muscle-preserving pharma arrives soon.** Bimagrumab plus semaglutide held lean mass loss to ~7% of total loss (Phase 2), while S-LITE showed liraglutide plus supervised training produced lean-mass gain ([AJMC](https://www.ajmc.com/view/glp-1-therapies-in-2026-beyond-blood-sugar-and-the-scale)). Until then, the non-drug muscle protocol is unowned.

## Idea seeds

- Post-GLP-1 maintenance and muscle "operating system" (nutrition, training, dose-taper, restart triggers) sold to employers and Medicare Advantage plans on persistence outcomes.
- Verified-supply and purity-testing layer for peptides and gray-market GLP-1s.
- Capped-cost GLP-1 benefit for employers (cash-pay pill plus coaching), replacing uncapped coverage.
- Care bundle for the newly uninsured or Medicaid-churned (low-cost cash-pay primary care plus a $149 GLP-1 pill).
- GLP-1-aware products for eating-disorder-risk screening and for alcohol-use programs.

# Briefing: Construction, Housing Shortage, Trades Labor, Home Services (as of 2026-09-28)

Caveat: several numbers come from vendor blogs or aggregator sites (flagged "vendor stat"). Cross-check before betting money on them.

## 1. Biggest shifts, last 12-18 months

- **The labor problem changed shape.** ABC now says construction must add [349,000 net workers in 2026 and 456,000 in 2027](https://www.abc.org/News-Media/News-Releases/abc-construction-industry-must-attract-349000-workers-in-2026-despite-macroeconomic-headwinds). That is down from 439,000 for 2025 and 500,000+ in earlier years, and most of it is retirements. NAHB puts the gap nearer [300,000](https://www.nahb.org/blog/2026/09/immigration-enforcement).
- **Immigration enforcement is the acute shock.** Immigrants are [over 25% of the construction workforce](https://www.nahb.org/blog/2026/09/immigration-enforcement). About 34% of trades workers are foreign-born, up to [61% in some trades](https://www.constructiondive.com/news/how-immigration-enforcement-will-impact-construction-in-2026/809482/). ICE arrests rose from 32,545 in May to [49,571 in July 2026](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/ice-enforcement-labor-costs/), with about 40% in Texas and Florida. Documented workers and citizens avoid sites too. One Minnesota roofing crew went from [80 workers to 6](https://www.axios.com/2026/09/22/home-builders-immigrant-workers-ice) while agents were nearby.
- **Data centers are absorbing electricians.** Data center work is now [nearly a third of the total shortage](https://www.classet.ai/blog/data-center-labor-shortage-2026). Journeymen on heavy overtime gross $130-170K (vendor stat). Texas homebuilders report [electrical delays of up to 2 months](https://www.planetizen.com/news/2026/05/137471-texas-data-centers-demand-electricians-delaying-housing-construction-2-months).
- **Housing shortage estimates disagree by 4x.** Zillow says [4.5-4.7M units](https://www.thestreet.com/real-estate/zillow-housing-shortage-update-analysis). Freddie Mac says [3.7M](https://www.resiclubanalytics.com/p/freddie-mac-housing-shortage-has-delayed-the-formation-of-1-million-households). NAHB says about 1.2M. Builders are not building into it.
- **Builders are financing shops now.** August starts were [1.275M SAAR, and completions fell 27.1% YoY](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/housing-starts-august-2026/). 63% of builders use incentives and 35% cut prices. 80-90% of new-home sales [need rate buydowns](https://www.rismedia.com/2026/09/17/housing-starts-more-like-stops-numbers-decline-august/), with 30-year rates near 7%. Forecasts have 2027 starts down 2-4%.
- **Tariffs.** Builders estimate [$10,900 per home](https://www.nahb.org/advocacy/top-priorities/building-materials-trade-policy/how-tariffs-impact-home-building). Brookings sees [about $30B](https://www.brookings.edu/articles/recent-tariffs-threaten-residential-construction/) added to residential construction and renovation cost by 2027. Only about 7% of inputs are imported, but those are mostly items with no quick domestic substitute. Reported lumber and steel tariff rates conflict across sources.
- **New law.** The [21st Century ROAD to Housing Act](https://mitsloan.mit.edu/centers-initiatives/mit-gcfp/21st-century-road-to-housing-what-congress-accomplished-2026-and-what-remains-to-be-done) became law on July 11, 2026. It:
  - kills the manufactured-home steel chassis rule (about $10K or 10% of unit cost);
  - streamlines environmental review for multifamily of 15 units or fewer;
  - funds standard duplex and townhome blueprints;
  - bars investors with more than 350 homes from buying existing houses.

  [HUD must still publish new standards](https://hoodline.com/2026/09/hud-s-national-mall-showcase-bets-on-factory-built-homes-to-fix-housing-crunch/) before chassis-optional homes ship. MIT's read is "modest at best" in the short run.
- **HVAC is at a cyclical trough.** 2025 residential shipments fell [25-50% YoY](https://www.thehardwirenews.com/hvac-market-correction-2026-data-rebound-2027/) after A2L pre-buying, with equipment prices about 40% above 2020. Carrier plans for 7.5M units versus a historical 9M. Rebound is expected in 2027. The tech shortage of about 110,000 persists, and A2L certification adds a qualification layer.

## 2. Acute, quantified pain points

- **Site continuity for small private builders.**
  - Austin framing costs rose 25-50%, adding $2-5K per home.
  - Foundations sit 30+ days waiting for crews. One executive described [15-20 houses stuck on foundations for 6+ weeks](https://www.housingwire.com/articles/ice-enforcement-labor-costs/).
  - A West Virginia builder is at risk of losing about 40 closings.
  - A typical home needs about two dozen subs, and loan interest keeps accruing.
- **Permit friction.** Honolulu residential permits average [218 days, commercial 469](https://www.hawaiipublicradio.org/local-news/2026-09-24/honolulu-building-permit-applications-rise-under-ai-processing-tools). A reported Aug 2026 paper claims a 25% cut in approval time could lift housing production about 24% (unverified).
- **Homeowners are waiting on quotes.** Angi's data: [73% of homeowners have unstarted projects](https://intercom.help/angi/en/articles/15972206-the-backlog-boom-73-of-homeowners-have-projects-waiting), 78% of them have no quotes yet, and 72% of postponers cite budget. The average project is $5,368. Barriers to hiring a pro: "too busy" 21%, trust 21%, no response 14%. Cash payment fell 57% to 51% and credit cards rose 27% to 30%. 62% now choose repair over replace, up from 51%.
- **Missed calls.** Invoca data puts about [48% of home-services calls as never reaching a person](https://www.fingerlakes1.com/2026/09/28/how-an-ai-receptionist-for-contractors-helps-plumbers-and-hvac-shops-stop-missing-calls/). A LeadAngel stat (vendor) says a 2-minute reply converts 62% of leads versus 28% at 42 minutes.
- **Cash flow.** GCs are [4x more likely than subs to be paid within 30 days](https://thebirmgroup.com/why-contractors-still-cant-find-workers-in-2026-and-whats-going-wrong/). One in five subs waits 60+ days.
- **Lead-gen distrust.** Angi/HomeAdvisor charges about $288-300 a year plus [$15-85 per lead](https://www.leadtruffle.co/blog/complete-guide-angi-leads-home-service-contractors-2026/), and the leads are shared with many bidders. There was an FTC settlement in 2023.
- **Aging stock.** Median home age is [44 years](https://www.jchs.harvard.edu/blog/remodeling-growth-set-downshift-late-2026), up from 28 in 1993. Remodeling spend hit a record $524B, but growth is slowing to about 1.6% by year-end.

## 3. Where money is flowing (and what is crowded)

- **PE roll-ups of trades.** [Apollo is putting about $2B into Apex at a roughly $10B valuation](https://profitabilitypartners.io/home-services-private-equity-acquirers/) (May 2026). Blackstone bought Champions in Feb 2026. Bain and Mubadala bought Service Logic in Dec 2025. Reported multiples are [10-14x EBITDA for platforms above $25M revenue versus 2-3.5x for small owner-operators](https://ctacquisitions.com/guides/private-equity-home-services-statistics-2026/). The same source scores roofing as the least consolidated trade.
- **Big-box vertical integration.** Home Depot bought SRS ($18B) and GMS, and [Mingledorff's (HVAC distribution) in May 2026](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/354950/000162828026019436/hd-20260201.htm). Lowe's bought [FBM for $8.8B](https://www.retaildive.com/news/lowes-acquire-foundation-building-materials-pro-business/758228/) and Artisan Design for $1.3B.
- **Physical AI for homebuilding.** TerraFirma raised a [$100M Series A led by Kleiner](https://bricks-bytes.com/funding-ma/latest-construction-technology-funding-rounds-7th-sep-2026/). Higharc raised a $95M Series C. Reframe Systems raised $40M (10 homes built, 114 planned). Monumental raised a [$32M Series B](https://www.deadfront.ai/blog/august-2026-ai-construction-roundup) for bricklaying robots.
- **Contech M&A.** Procore-Datagrid, Autodesk-Rhumbix, Trimble-Document Crunch, and Nemetschek-HCSS are all in [one Construction Dive roundup](https://www.constructiondive.com/news/merger-acquistion-roundup-construction-tech-autodesk-trimble/818155/). Procore now ships 20 pre-built agents.
- **Crowded:** AI takeoff and estimating, GC project-management agents, contract review, AI phone receptionists (many vendors), and permit-review platforms sold to governments.

## 4. Underserved segments and structural gaps

- **Solo to 5-tech shops and sub-$10K jobs.** ServiceTitan is the category leader. After its Q2 (Sept 2026) it fell [about 26%](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-servicetitan-sinks-after-q2-2026-results-and-outlook-93CH-4892559) on GTV growth slowing to 17%, softer HVAC leads, and a decision to delay new commercial trades and residential exteriors. It expects only about 700 locations on its agentic "Max" tier by fiscal year-end, so most tiny shops have no AI operations layer.
- **Roofing and exteriors.** They are the least PE-consolidated trade and the one ServiceTitan just deprioritized.
- **Exit market for sub-$5M trade shops.** [McKinsey](https://www.forbes.com/sites/alisoncoleman/2026/01/14/the-silver-tsunami-is-reshaping-small-business-why-exit-planning-cant-wait/): 6M SMBs face ownership transitions by 2035. A third of owners over 50 struggle to find a buyer. Roll-ups mostly skip shops at that scale, which is a 3-5x valuation gap.
- **Applicant-side permit work.** Government AI (Denver's [$4.6M five-year contract](https://stateline.org/2026/08/20/cities-turn-to-ai-to-speed-housing-permitting/), Honolulu CivCheck) serves reviewers. Small builders, ADU owners and rural jurisdictions have few tools.
- **Sub-tier labor compliance.** NAHB is asking that employers' verification duty be limited to direct employees, not subcontractors' workers. Builders currently lack reliable tools for crew continuity and verification across two dozen subs.
- **Site work for factory-built homes.** Chassis-optional homes still need foundations, utility hookups, set crews and local financing, all of which stay local and human.
- **Incumbents that cannot fix this.** Angi's economics rely on reselling the same lead to many pros. Home Depot cannot neutrally serve competing contractors. PE platforms rarely touch tiny shops. Governments cannot build advocacy tools for applicants.

## 5. Weird signals

- **Faster permit review, bigger backlog.** Honolulu says review cycles are down 58% and review time down 55%. Yet applications rose 34% while permits issued rose only 5%, and the [backlog is 9,252](https://www.hawaiipublicradio.org/local-news/2026-09-24/honolulu-building-permit-applications-rise-under-ai-processing-tools). Cheaper filing may induce demand, so the bottleneck moves downstream (inspections, post-permit, contractors).
- **Starts are steady but completions fell 27.1%.** The binding constraint may now be finishing homes (subs, financing, rate buydowns), not starting them.
- **The trades "boom" is partly an illusion.** A Quartz headline of "+1,421% trade school enrollment" is called ["a demographic mirage"](https://qz.com/trade-school-enrollment-1421-percent-gen-z-explained-071026) (page returned 403; this is from the search snippet). Other claims, such as Gen Z at 31% of new apprentices and a 48% rise since 2021, are single-source. The pipeline may be thinner than the headlines suggest.
- **ICE and data centers hit the same bottleneck.** Both remove the same scarce, verified, skilled crews from homebuilding. The price signal (data center overtime versus $500K-home framing budgets) is pulling labor away from housing.
- **Customers like blended work.** DIY-only fell from 50% to 39% while "homeowner plus pro" rose from 27% to 46% (Angi). That suggests demand for unbundled, part-time pro help, not full-service jobs.

# Briefing: Labor-market disruption from AI (displaced white-collar workers, new job types, freelancing)
As of 2026-09-28. Scout: work-displacement. File: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/7d5d40b9-c4a2-5a88-8ca2-c003de06ceb9/scratchpad/biz/briefs/work-displacement.md

**Method caveat.** The WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) before my first query ran, so this briefing rests on WebFetch of primary and semi-primary pages plus the Hacker News Algolia API (practitioner threads). WebFetch answers come from a small summarizer model, so treat exact figures as "reported, verify before relying". CNBC, Quartz, Wired, Upwork Research and Reddit were blocked, so several items below are headline-only, and I say so.

## 1. Biggest shifts (last 12-18 months)
- **The damage is a hiring freeze for the young, not mass firing.** Stanford Digital Economy Lab ("Canaries in the Coal Mine", Aug 2026 revision, ADP payroll data through June 2026): employment for ages 22-25 in AI-exposed occupations is **19% below** where it would be versus less-exposed peers. The gap has widened steadily since first documented in Aug 2025. Authors find no economy-wide displacement. The effect runs through reduced hiring, concentrated where AI substitutes for work. Where AI complements, employment is flat or rising, especially for experienced workers. https://digitaleconomy.stanford.edu/publications/canaries-in-the-coal-mine/
- **Recent grads:** NY Fed 2026Q2 shows recent-grad unemployment of about 5.6% and **underemployment of 42%** (rising vs Q1). https://www.newyorkfed.org/research/college-labor-market
- **Global pattern:** Rest of World (Dec 2025) cites a 50%+ drop in fresh-grad hires at major tech firms over three years. Only 7% of 2024 new tech hires were recent grads. Junior tech postings fell about 35% in major EU countries in 2024. Indian IT services cut entry roles 20-25%. https://restofworld.org/2025/engineering-graduates-ai-job-losses/
- **Macro is low-fire, low-hire.** BLS Aug 2026: unemployment 4.1%, payrolls +162k, but information-sector employment fell 23k in one month vs an 8k/month average over the prior 12. https://www.bls.gov/news.release/empsit.nr0.htm
- **Big-corporate moves:** Amazon cut about 16,000 corporate roles (Jan 28, 2026, framed as anti-bureaucracy). https://www.cnbc.com/2026/01/28/amazon-layoffs-anti-bureaucracy-ai.html A follow-up Amazon story reports **rehiring laid-off workers into AI roles** (Quartz, Sep 23, 2026, headline only).
- **Wage split:** Indeed Hiring Lab (Sep 17, 2026) says advertised pay is rising fastest in the occupations most exposed to AI. A Sep 24 economist survey expects AI to weigh most on degree-holders' pay over the next year. https://hiringlab.indeed.com/

## 2. Quantified pain points (practitioner voice)
- **Job-search grind, HN "Is the Job Market Actually Bad?" (138 pts, 211 comments, May 2026):** one commenter with 5 years' experience sent 65 applications in a month and got 3 phone screens and 0 interviews. Another got 1 HR screen in 4 months despite a MAG7 resume. Others report 13 months to find work after an HR layoff, and 7 months ending in "a big step back". Consensus: referrals beat cold applications, and ATS filtering is aggressive. https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47988268
- **Despair signals:** "Ask HN: How Do I Get over My Existential Crisis?" (106 pts): hundreds to thousands of applications, junior dev stuck. "Pivot from SWE to What?" (49 pts, Dec 2025). "Ask HN: 10-year dev, tried earning on the side for a year, lost $2,200" (Mar 2026) shows the side-hustle escape hatch is not working either.
- **Hiring process is broken on both sides:** "How do you interview devs in a post-AI world?" (47 pts, Sep 19, 2026). "Interview questions assume candidates can afford Claude Code Max" (LeadDev, Aug 2026). An AI interviewer flagged a candidate's "habitual" use of Chrome (CBC, Feb 2026). Meta now lets candidates use AI in coding tests (Wired, Jul 2025).
- **Gig data workers are unhappy:** contractors report "declining pay", a "stressful work environment" and "inhumane working conditions" at Mercor (Verge, NY Mag, Wired coverage; HN May 12, 2026). A class action alleges Surge AI misclassified annotators (May 2025). Wired (Apr 29, 2026): "Workers Training Meta's AI Could Be Laid Off" (Covalen contractors).

## 3. Where the money is flowing (and what is crowded)
- **Human-data / expert-labor marketplaces are the hot spot.** Mercor: $350M Series C at **$10B** (Oct 2025). Reported gross run rate rose from $500M (Sep 2025) to $1B (early 2026) to **$2B (Jun 2026)**. Reported contractor payout is 60-70% of gross, implying $600-800M net. It claims nearly 5M expert contractors across physics, finance, IB, law, medicine and consulting. Top buyers are five frontier labs. The source is runtimewire, a lower-tier outlet, so verify. https://runtimewire.com/article/as-amazon-lets-mechanical-turk-fade-mercor-hits-a-2-billion-gross-run-rate
- **Peers:** Handshake gross run rate about $1.1B (Apr 2026, same source). Surge AI reported $1.2B revenue in 2024 with about 110 staff and about 1M annotators, and valuation talks of $15-25B in Jul 2025 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surge_AI).
- **Incumbent freelance marketplaces are shrinking.** Upwork: 2025 revenue $787.8M, net income down 46% to $115.4M, active clients down year over year to 763k (Jun 2026), and a second layoff of 25% in May 2026 (stock about -19%). It is pivoting to enterprise staffing and compliance via the Bubty and Ascen acquisitions (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upwork). Fiverr: 2025 revenue $431M, net income $21M, launched "Fiverr Go" AI features, and bought Digis (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiverr). Both figures come from Wikipedia, so verify.
- **Crowded:** AI interviewers and recruiting (Fika Jobs raised $4M in Jun 2026, https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/23/fika-jobs-raises-4m-to-build-a-video-first-hiring-platform-where-ai-agents-interview-candidates/, plus a dozen Show HN clones). Also resume tailoring, mock-interview bots, and freelancer proposal/contract tools (Proposly, Accordio).

## 4. Underserved segments and structural gaps
- **The expert-gig worker has no infrastructure.** Marketplaces keep 30-40% and profit from low payouts and easy contractor churn, so they will not build worker-side protections. Open gaps:
  - Portable reputation and credentials.
  - Income smoothing and benefits for irregular AI-training work.
  - IP clearance (Apr 2026 HN: Mercor offering to pay for prior work "employers might own").
  - Identity and data-breach insurance (Mercor's LiteLLM-linked breach: about 4TB, about 40k contractors' voice samples, Meta paused work, class actions).
- **The missing bottom rung.** If AI absorbs the tasks juniors used to learn on, employers will not train them and universities cannot teach fast enough. Nobody sells "supervised apprenticeship on real AI-assisted work" with a verifiable track record.
- **Verified skill signal.** Cold applications are dead, referrals dominate, AI-assisted tests are unreliable, and interviews are degraded. A trust or proof-of-work layer for mid-career and junior candidates is unaddressed. Incumbent job boards profit from application volume, so they are structurally conflicted.
- **Regret and repair market.** Headlines say employers who cut for AI are reversing (CNBC, Jul 1, 2026, headline only). Untested opportunities include AI-cleanup contractors, alumni and "boomerang" rehire networks, and workflow-audit services.
- **Mid-career displaced pros** (HR, ops, marketing, support) with domain judgment but no clear route into AI-supervision, QA or domain-expert work.

## 5. Weird signals
1. **AI leads the layoff-reason chart, but the volume is small.** Challenger listed AI as the top reason for five straight months through July 2026 (10,970 cuts in July). Total announced cuts YTD through Aug were 529,914, **down 41%** YoY, and August (52,881) was the lowest August since 2022. Restructuring retook the top spot. July hiring plans (16,095) were the highest July on record. AI is partly a narrative and cover story. https://www.challengergray.com/blog/category/job-cuts-report/
2. **Barbell labor market:** experienced workers in AI-exposed occupations see rising advertised pay while 22-25-year-olds in the same occupations trail by 19%.
3. **Mercor's run rate quadrupled in about nine months** as Amazon Mechanical Turk fades, while its contractors complain of falling pay. White-collar expertise is being turned into a commodity input.
4. **A "no-AI-enforced dev jobs" niche.** Ask HN (Jun 27, 2026): a developer says they were laid off for "misalignment" after questioning AI mandates. Commenters predict a premium for developers who are not AI-dependent, and some orgs ban agentic tools for code-exfiltration reasons. Weak but real.
5. **Agent-labor marketplaces.** 47jobs ("a Fiverr/Upwork for AI agents", 20 pts and 52 comments, Sep 2025) and Hirenewtalent.ai ("hire offshore in minutes via API", Aug 2026) show humans and agents converging on the same marketplaces. Also "Laid-Off Developers Create AI Model to Replace CEOs" (PCMag, Sep 10, 2026).

## Idea-seeds (for downstream screening, not endorsements)
- Worker-side "union-lite" for AI expert contractors: benefits, IP clearance, breach insurance, portable rating.
- Paid apprenticeship marketplace where juniors QA and supervise AI work under senior review and earn verifiable credentials.
- Boomerang and rehire network for AI-washed layoffs.
- Anti-application-spam trust layer: verified proof-of-work portfolios plus employer-paid referrals.
- Directory and insurer for "no-AI-mandate" engineering employers.

- **Record buyer's market.** August 2026 was the strongest buyer's market since Redfin's 2013 records, with 58% more sellers than buyers. 44.7% of sales included seller concessions (Atlanta 72.8%, San Jose 4.2%), and 15.8% had both a price cut and concessions ([Redfin](https://www.redfin.com/news/press-releases/nearly-half-of-homebuyers-get-concessions-from-sellers-as-most-markets-tip-in-buyers-favor/), [Redfin HPI](https://www.redfin.com/news/home-price-index-august-2026/)). National prices are still +3.7% YoY, but the split is huge: San Francisco +12%, Chicago +9.2%, Dallas -1.4%, Austin -1.0%.
- **The rental supply wave has crested.** National median rent is $1,388, -0.4% YoY, with 7.0% vacancy (peak 7.3% in Feb) and 34 days to lease, the longest September since 2019 ([Apartment List](https://www.apartmentlist.com/research/national-rent-data)). Aug multifamily starts fell 15.5% YoY and completions fell 35.7%, while input costs are +8.9% ([Multifamily Dive](https://www.multifamilydive.com/news/multifamily-starts-apartment-construction-august/830679/)). 1.2M units remain in lease-up (peak 1.4M), and concessions run 15.8% of stabilized units (South 21.1%, Austin 37%) ([Multifamily Dive](https://www.multifamilydive.com/news/multifamily-lease-ups-rent-growth/830227/)).
- **Office is bifurcating.** National vacancy is 17.8%, down 90bp YoY, and asking rent is $33.20 (+1.7%). Manhattan is about 10% and San Francisco 25.9%. 32.4M sf is under construction, concentrated in gateway markets ([CommercialEdge](https://www.commercialcafe.com/blog/national-office-report/)). Office CMBS delinquency hit 13.2%, the highest since at least 2019, with 15.7% in special servicing and $39B maturing in 12 months. 71% of distressed balance is refinance failure, not missed payments ([Commercial Observer](https://commercialobserver.com/2026/09/office-cmbs-delinquency-rate-cred-iq/)). $289B of loans on 14,000 office properties mature by 2028.
- **Conversions are moving to public land and affordable mandates.** NYC's 100 Gold Street grew from 3,700 to 4,000 units (1,000 affordable) on city-owned land, fast-tracked by the Mamdani administration ([Commercial Observer](https://commercialobserver.com/2026/09/100-gold-street-conversion-housing-mamdani/)).
- **Regulatory stack:**
  - RealPage/DOJ: Pinnacle signed a consent decree Sept 4, and Camden is the only original defendant left unsettled ([Multifamily Dive](https://www.multifamilydive.com/news/doj-pinnacle-settlement-realpage-lawsuit/830108/)). Private settlements exceed $500M ([tracker](https://www.multifamilydive.com/news/algorithmic-rent-pricing-lawsuit-tracker/826178/)). New York State (Dec 2025) and Berkeley ban pricing algorithms. San Diego's ordinance carries $1,000 per violation, and a UDR class action was filed under it ([Multifamily Dive](https://www.multifamilydive.com/news/udr-rent-pricing-class-action-lawsuit-san-diego/827109/)).

## 2. Acute, quantified pain

- **Wage-rent gap.** A typical retail worker earns $34,436 vs $71,172 needed for a typical $1,779 apartment (Redfin, 2025 data) ([Redfin](https://www.redfin.com/news/retail-worker-rental-affordability-2025/)).

# Briefing: Parenting, Childcare Deserts, Gen Alpha, Kids x AI/Screens (as of 2026-09-28)

**Method caveat (read first):** The session's WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) before I could run any searches, and I did not route around it. This briefing rests on about 25 direct WebFetch reads. Most are Wikipedia, which is secondary and sometimes stale or wrong. A few are primary (FTC, Child Care Aware, CAP). Items tagged **[bg]** come from my background knowledge (cutoff June 2026) and were not re-verified in this run. Items tagged **[shaky]** look internally inconsistent and need checking. No Reddit or forum data could be pulled (fetch blocked), so the "practitioner pain" section is thin.

## 1. Biggest shifts, last 12-18 months

- **Under-16 social media bans went from theory to a global wave.** Per [Wikipedia: age verification laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_media_age_verification_laws):
  - Australia took effect 2025-12-10 (10 platforms incl. YouTube, Reddit, Twitch, Kick). More than 310k child accounts were deactivated by March 2026.
  - Brazil took effect 2026-03-17 and Indonesia 2026-03-28 (also covers Roblox). Malaysia took effect 2026-06-01, using eKYC.
  - The UK has had age checks since 2025-07-25 and has a fuller under-16 ban pending (spring 2027).
  - US states:
    - Florida: under-14 ban, parental consent for 14-15.
    - Texas: app-store age verification, effective 2026-06-04.
    - Ohio: consent for under-16s, effective 2026-06-18.
  - Reported account terminations of "4.7 million" appear for both Brazil and Indonesia **[shaky]**.
- **The bans are leaky, so the opportunity is in enforcement and substitutes.** Per [the Australian Act page](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Online_Safety_Amendment_(Social_Media_Minimum_Age)_Act_2024):
  - By Feb 2026, "many children" had worked around the ban. VPNs cost under A$20/month.
  - The government began investigating Facebook, Instagram, Snapchat, TikTok and YouTube in March 2026 (fines up to A$49.5M).
  - By June 2026 the PM proposed doubling fines to about A$99M and extending eSafety powers to app stores and age-assurance providers.
  - Support fell from 69% (Jul 2024) to 57% (Dec 2025). Only 29% of parents planned full compliance. 75% of surveyed youth planned to keep using the platforms.
- **Age assurance is becoming OS-level infrastructure.** California's Digital Age Assurance Act (signed Oct 2025) and similar late-2025 laws require operating systems to store date of birth and expose an age-attestation API ([source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Age_verification_system)). Roblox went to mandatory age checks (Dec 2025 in some countries, global Jan 2026), then a June 2026 tier split: Roblox Kids (<9), Select (9-15), standard (16+) ([source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roblox)). Persona reportedly runs Roblox's facial age estimation and drew user complaints. A 2026 IDScan breach ("150M+ licenses") is reported **[shaky]**. Breaches show that ID-based age checks carry a privacy liability.
- **Kids and AI companions became a regulated, litigated category.**
  - The FTC issued 6(b) orders on 2025-09-11 to Alphabet, Character.AI, Instagram, Meta, OpenAI, Snap and xAI, covering minors' harms, COPPA compliance and age enforcement ([FTC](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/09/ftc-launches-inquiry-ai-chatbots-acting-companions)).
  - Character.AI barred under-18s from open-ended chat from 2025-11-25. Pennsylvania sued it in May 2026 over bots posing as licensed clinicians ([source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Character.ai)).
  - Raine v. OpenAI (Aug 2025) opened a wave of wrongful-death suits ([source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raine_v._OpenAI)).
  - California SB 243 and a New York law require AI disclosure and self-harm safeguards. Common Sense Media found 72% of US teens have used AI companions and over half use them regularly ([source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AI_companion)).
- **US federal law is stuck but moving.** KOSA passed the Senate 91-3 in 2024. A June 2026 House deal drops "duty of care" and preempts state laws, with Democratic pushback. The KIDS Act (Dec 2025) bundles age verification with AI chatbot controls ([source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kids_Online_Safety_Act)). COPPA 2.0 reportedly passed the Senate unanimously in March 2026 ([source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children%27s_Online_Privacy_Protection_Act)). The amended COPPA Rule requires separate opt-in for third-party sharing, retention limits and biometric coverage, with a compliance deadline about April 2026 ([FTC](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/01/ftc-finalizes-changes-childrens-privacy-rule-limiting-companies-ability-monetize-kids-data)).
- **Tax and policy tailwinds for childcare and family finance** ([OBBBA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One_Big_Beautiful_Bill_Act)):
  - Dependent-care FSA limit rose from $5,000 to $7,500.
  - The 45F employer childcare credit rose to 40% (50% for small businesses), capped at $500k ($600k for small businesses), from 2026-01-01.
  - Child tax credit is $2,200.
  - "Trump Accounts" pay $1,000 per child born 2025-2028, and deposits opened 2026-07-04.
- **School phone bans went mainstream:** 12 US states have enacted them, Oregon reports 99% of districts implementing, and 40% of countries had bans by 2024 ([source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mobile_phones_in_schools)).

## 2. Acute, quantified pain points

- **Price:**
  - Average US childcare is **$13,128/yr** (2024), up 29% since 2020 vs 22% general inflation.
  - It takes 10% of median income for married couples and **35% for single parents**. The federal "affordable" standard is 7%.
  - Two children in center care cost more than rent in every state and more than a mortgage in 45 states ([Child Care Aware, May 2025](https://www.childcareaware.org/price-landscape/)).
- **Workforce paradox:** the average childcare worker earns **$33,140**, so care for two kids costs 44-100%+ of their own wage. Supply is barely growing: centers +1.5% and family homes +4.3% in 2024 (same source).
- **Desert definition:** CAP defines a desert as 3+ children under 6 per licensed slot ([CAP](https://www.americanprogress.org/feature/child-care-deserts)). The bigger point is that the licensed-slot map is the wrong unit. Parents actually cobble together informal care (grandparents, nannies, nanny shares), which is unmeasured and unmanaged.
- **Trust and safety in care:** repeated abuse incidents at premium chains (Bright Horizons NYC 2025; a former employee sentenced to 18 years in 2026, per [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bright_Horizons)). Parents lack any verified real-time quality signal beyond cameras.
- **Parents cannot verify what is inside their kid's AI:** 72% teen companion use, lawsuits over AI posing as licensed professionals, and AI toys documented **[bg]** giving inappropriate content in late-2025 consumer testing (PIRG "Trouble in Toyland"; page blocked, unverified this run).
- **Age-gating friction:** compliance costs land on every app and game studio with under-18 users. Parents face repeated ID uploads. Kids evade with VPNs and borrowed IDs.

## 3. Where money is flowing (and crowding)

- **Crowded or consolidated:** center-based chains (KinderCare ~1,250 centers and ~200k kids/day, [NYSE: KLC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KinderCare); Bright Horizons, ~1,000+ centers). Age-verification vendors (Persona, Yoti, AU10TIX, VerifyMy and others). Parental-control apps (Bark, Qustodio, Life360, Apple/Google native controls). Kids' AI tutors (Khanmigo and many others).
- **Big-corporate moves:**
  - Mattel is restructuring around media and games (Mattel Studios June 2025, Game Studios Aug 2026, Mattel163 fully acquired 2026) ([source](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mattel)).
  - **[bg]** Mattel-OpenAI partnership (June 2025).
  - **[bg]** Character.AI's Google licensing deal (2024, about $2.7B).
- **Employer demand is subsidized:** the 45F credit jump (above) plus DCFSA at $7,500 give employers and families new reasons to buy childcare benefits, with a 2026 effective date, so early sales cycles are open now.

## 4. Underserved segments and structural gaps

- **Informal/"cobbled" care operations:** no software layer for the grandparent, nanny-share or micro-pod economy. Licensed chains cannot serve it. Regulation follows licensed slots only.
- **Single parents at 35% of income** cannot use DCFSA well (no employer or tax capacity). Fintech and benefit design has not caught up.
- **Age assurance for the 8-15 band:** platforms need privacy-preserving, non-ID age and parent-consent signals.   - Funeral homes lack modern software and staff.

## 3. Where the money is flowing
- **Consolidators are healthy [V].** SCI Q2'26 revenue was $1,103.3M (+4%). Average revenue per service was $5,985 (+3.3%). Preneed funeral production rose 7% and cemetery preneed rose 8%. Operating cash flow was $238.7M (+43%), and 2026 cash flow guidance was raised to about $1,085M. Volume fell 1.4%, and pricing and preneed are doing the work. Everstory Partners (stonemor.com now redirects there) calls itself the #2 US deathcare company. It reports 460+ providers in 23 states plus Puerto Rico and about 66K families per year. It has digitized about 400 cemeteries with drone mapping and bought Franklin Memorial Park in June 2026. [everstorypartners.com](https://www.everstorypartners.com/)
- **Fragmentation [V].** NFDA counts 15,401 US funeral homes, about 75% family or privately owned. The funeral sector is $16.3B in revenue with 105,300 employees, plus about $4.3B from crematories and cemeteries. [NFDA](https://nfda.org/news/statistics) The top six operators hold an estimated 25-30% share. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_care_industry_in_the_United_States)
- **Insurer and employer channel [V].** Empathy has raised $162M+ and claims 50M+ covered policyholders and 9M+ covered employees. Partners include MetLife, New York Life, Allianz, Aflac, Munich Re and TIAA. Products are loss support, LifeVault, caregiving and bereavement leave. [empathy.com](https://www.empathy.com/about)
- **Insurtech [V].** Ethos IPO'd on Nasdaq (LIFE) on Jan 29, 2026 at about a $1.2B valuation, versus $2.7B in 2021. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethos_Technologies)
- **Life settlements [V].** About 10M policies lapse per year against a market of about 3.2K policies and $4.6B face in 2020. Coventry Direct and Abacus Life were the largest buyers as of 2025. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life_settlement)
- **Crowded:** online wills and trusts, preneed and funeral financing, direct cremation, bereavement benefits (B2B2C), insurtech life. Life-settlement buyers are also crowded.
- **Private banks [V]:** Cerulli (Sept 1, 2026) frames alternatives as a retention tool. 89% of surveyed firms say family meetings are essential during transitions. Wealth managers are already targeting the heir cohort.

## 4. Underserved gaps and structural blind spots
- **Middle-class estates.** Wealth managers chase the $62T from the top 2%. Estates of $200K-$2M, which are mostly a house plus a retirement account, get either a $400/hr attorney or nothing. Those estates are where the executor's workload is heaviest relative to the help available.
- **Executor operations after death.** Empathy handles notifications through insurers. The dedicated "estate close-out" workflow (accounts, property, taxes, distribution) has no dominant software owner. Trust & Will treats probate as an add-on [V].
- **Widows.** About $40T flows to widowed women [V]. Those women are the ones executing an estate while grieving, and advisor firms rarely serve them well [B].
- **Consolidators structurally cannot:** cut prices, since 3.7%/yr price increases and 58% cremation define their margins. They also cannot recommend competitors, and they market preneed to profit from the float.
- **Independent cemeteries** (about 115,000 in 2016 [V], [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_care_industry_in_the_United_States)) are mostly undigitized, while #2 operator Everstory says it has digitized about 400 of its own. Plot records, deeds and maps are a data problem.
- **Logistics arbitrage.** Recompose claims to serve all 50 states, so remains travel to Washington state [V]. That is a shipping and coordination business where legality is fragmented.

## 5. Weird signals
1. **Lonely-death economy in Japan [V].** In H1 2024, 37,227 people living alone were found dead at home. Nearly 4,000 were undiscovered for over a month, and 130 for a year or more. 70% were 65+. One Osaka moving company says 20% of its jobs (about 300 a year) are removing belongings after lonely deaths. South Korea has the same pattern (godoksa). [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kodokushi) The US analog, solo agers with no heirs, has no equivalent service layer [B].
2. **Preneed decouples from volume [V].** SCI's preneed sales were up 7-8% while services fell 1.4% and cash flow rose 43%. Funeral pricing power is in prepaid contracts, not at-need decisions, and that contract book is a regulatory target.
3. **First UK NHS request to freeze a corpse (2026) [V].** About 600 people are cryopreserved worldwide as of 2024. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryonics) A tiny tail, but cryonics handling is moving into ordinary hospital procedure.
4. **Consumer appetite outruns supply [V].** NFDA says 61.4% of consumers are interested in green options (up from 55.7% in 2021), and 58.3% have attended services at unconventional venues. Legal supply is still limited to 14 states for composting and hydrolysis's utility permit problems. [NFDA](https://nfda.org/news/statistics)
5. **Griefbots are unregulated but researched [V/B].** Known products include HereAfter, Project December and Eternime. Scholars are calling for oversight. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Griefbot) I found no regulation or 2026 legal cases in this session.
